Where is Dorchester County and how big is it?

Dorchester County is on Maryland's Mid-Eastern Shore, with Cambridge as the county seat and largest city. It is the largest Maryland county by area and the least densely populated.

The county covers 983 square miles, and 442 of them (45 percent) are water. It borders the Choptank River to the north, Talbot and Caroline counties, Wicomico County, Sussex County in Delaware and the Chesapeake Bay on the west. Much of it is marsh, forest and farmland, and the county's own slogan is The Heart of Chesapeake Country.

The county was formed in 1669 and named for the Earl of Dorset. Harriet Tubman was born here. The 2020 census counted 32,531 people, with a median age of 45.1, and the 2025 estimate is 33,628.

What is Cambridge like for a home seller?

Cambridge sits on the south bank of the Choptank River at about 20 feet above sea level, and it had 13,096 residents in 2020. It was incorporated in 1793, and part of its downtown was declared a historic district in 1990.

Canning built the town. Phillips Packing Company employed up to 10,000 people at its peak and closed completely by the early 1960s, which left lasting unemployment. The Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay resort opened in 2002 with 400 rooms, a golf course and a marina, and Cambridge became a Maryland Main Street community on July 1, 2003.

  • U.S. Route 50 runs through the city, and the eastern stretch is called Sunburst Highway.
  • Cambridge-Dorchester Airport is a county-owned general aviation field southeast of town with a 4,477 foot runway.
  • The Cambridge Historic District covers Wards I and III in the northwest, and the Pine Street Neighborhood Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Of the city's 6,464 housing units, 13.9 percent were vacant at the 2020 census. Owners of a vacant house there still owe the same tax and carry the same upkeep.

What drives the Dorchester County economy?

Water and farmland have long been the base of the Dorchester County economy. Many residents were historically watermen and farmers, and the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries supply crabs, oysters and many fish species to commercial and recreational fishermen.

Horn Point Laboratory in the Cambridge area is home to the largest oyster hatchery on the East Coast. A 4.3 megawatt solar farm in Cambridge supplies about 40 percent of the power for the National Aquarium in Baltimore.

The county works under a charter home rule government with a five-member council. With only about 33,600 residents countywide, a seller works with a small local buyer pool.

How much of Dorchester County is in a flood zone?

How is Dorchester County property tax billed and collected?

Dorchester County bills in July, and the annual bill and the first semiannual installment are due September 30, with the second installment due December 31. The county collects real property tax for every municipality in the county.

Payment options listed by the county include the online Tax and Utility Bill portal run through a vendor, mail, and an in-person visit to the County Office Building at 501 Court Lane in Cambridge. The county main number is 410-228-1700, and the state's list of billing offices shows the Department of Finance at 410-228-4343. The county's page for the office notes closures for Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day and Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

After the due dates pass, unpaid accounts accrue interest and a penalty, and the lien can move toward the county's tax sale. Ask the finance office for a payoff figure on the exact day you plan to close, since interest runs monthly.

Dorchester County runs its tax sale online, and in 2025 bidding opened at noon on June 16 and closed at noon on June 17. The state's 2026 schedule lists Dorchester County on May 19, so confirm the date with the finance office.

  • Bidders registered online, and the registration fee was $50.
  • An owner could stop a sale by paying in full by 4:00 p.m. on June 12, 2025.
  • Owners also owe a $50 advertising fee per property and interest as the law provides.

State guidance adds that owners can redeem until a court forecloses, and that a buyer can ask for foreclosure after six months, or nine months for an owner-occupied home. The certificate is void if no foreclosure case is filed in two years.

What can you appeal or claim on a Dorchester County property?

Dorchester County owners use the same state appeal ladder as everyone in Maryland, and the first step has a 45 day deadline from the notice date. SDAT normally reassesses property every three years and mails a Notice of Assessment.

After the Supervisor of Assessments, an owner can go to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days, then to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order. In the years between reassessments, a petition for review is due by the first working day after January 1. A buyer of a house transferred between January 1 and June 30 has 60 days from the transfer, once the deed is recorded.

Can I sell a Dorchester County house before the tax sale?

Yes, if you pay the tax and fees before the cutoff the house comes off the sale list, and a closing can pay the balance from proceeds. In 2025 the payment deadline was June 12 at 4:00 p.m., so ask the finance office for the current date.
